samples.summary: No test covers "latest CI run wins" — the re-run sort in ciPassed is unexercised
samples.evidence: The new test "gate 1 reads the run NAMED 'CI'" pins the `r.name === "CI"` filter but never gives two CI runs with different `created_at`. Across the whole suite every config has at most one `{name: "CI", ...}` entry (mark-ready.test.mjs:89, 174-176, 193, 205); the second run in the new test is named `agent-review-panel` and is filtered out before the sort. So `runs.sort((a,b) => new Date(b.created_at) - new Date(a.created_at))` at mark-ready.mjs:136 has no coverage: inverting the comparator (or dropping the sort) keeps every test green while an OLD green CI run stands in for a NEWER red one, promoting a PR whose CI actually failed — exactly the unforgeable-evidence guard this file exists to enforce.

samples.summary: The rewritten promote-step shell is only regex-matched as text, never executed, and no shellcheck/actionlint lane exists
samples.evidence: "agent-review-panel.yml handles every mark-ready code" asserts on the YAML string (window/case/branch regexes, lines 329-415). Nothing runs the script body, so a shell-level defect the diff could introduce — an unbalanced quote or brace in the new `case`, an unset `$RUNNER_TEMP`, a grep whose log path differs from the redirect target — satisfies every assertion and only surfaces on a live promote run. `grep -rn 'actionlint\|shellcheck'` finds no CI lane for workflow shell, so text matching is the only check that exists. A cheap harness (feed a fixture log + a fake `$code` to `bash -c` on the extracted block) would turn these into behavioral tests.

samples.summary: `cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log"` — the whole reason the redirect is not a data loss — has no assertion
samples.evidence: The diff redirects mark-ready's output away from the step log and justifies it with "`cat` afterwards puts the report back in the step log, where it was before" (yml:1495-1497, 1503). The workflow test asserts the redirect (`assert.match(invocation, />\s*"\$RUNNER_TEMP\/mark-ready\.log" 2>&1/)`, test:362) but never asserts the log is echoed back. Deleting the `cat` line passes the entire suite while every promote run loses the gate report — the only human-readable output of this job — silently.
searchedFor: read the full workflow assertion test

samples.summary: `set +e` around the invocation is unasserted, although the entire exit-code contract depends on it
samples.evidence: GitHub's default shell is `bash -e {0}`, so without `set +e` (yml:1498) the step aborts at the non-zero exit before `code=$?` runs and the benign exit-1 "leaving as draft" outcome becomes a red job. The test asserts `code=$?` exists (test:359-360) and that the capture is not a pipe (test:363) but never that error-exit is disabled around it, so removing `set +e` — or moving `set -e` above `code=$?` — keeps the suite green.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. mark-ready.mjs:133-137 filters workflow_runs to name==="CI", then sorts by created_at desc and reads runs[0].conclusion — the sort only matters with 2+ CI-named runs. Every workflowRuns fixture in scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs produces at most ONE CI-named run: okConfig (line 89) has one green CI; lines 172-176 have [], one red CI, one null CI; the new "gate 1 reads the run NAMED 'CI'" test (lines 189-206) pairs the CI run with {name:"agent-review-panel"} (line 189), which the name filter drops before the sort; line 409 uses []. Inverting or deleting the comparator keeps all of them green. Searched wider: workflowRuns/workflow_runs appears in no other non-node_modules test file; no other test file spawns mark-ready.mjs; ciPassed is a file-local, non-exported function in a CLI that the test header (lines 15-20) documents as untestable by import; the only source-census assertion (lines 309-327) covers process.exit literals, not the sort. The .trusted baseline test (lines 81,149,150) has the same single-CI-run fixtures, so no counterexample there either. The gap is over the unforgeable CI-evidence gate, whose silent failure would promote a PR whose latest CI run was red.
